subject: Neptune Analytics — international transfer plan & subprocessor schedule
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neptune-analytics.com, Neptune Legal <privacy@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask: subprocessors, UK addendum, and TIA summary for procurement review

Hi Stephanie / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — procurement and legal have a few items they need to complete the security and privacy review for our contract team. Can you please provide the following by EOD Wednesday (20 Jan):

- Current list of subprocessors (host + infra + monitoring) with locations and last-assessed dates
- A one-page summary of transfer safeguards you rely on (SCCs, UK IDTA/UK addendum, TIAs/DTIAs) and which flows they cover
- Redline-ready UK addendum if you have one (we may run this by our counsel)
- Any outstanding supplier-side attestations (SOC 2 cert + date, encryption at rest/in transit statement)

Procurement is also asking for a short mutual action plan (M.A.P.) to show milestones before signature (e.g., finalize DPA, complete legal review, complete procurement checks).

If you want to kick off a quick call with legal, they are available Wednesday 11:00–12:00 PT.

Appreciate it — Lisa

--
Lisa Chen
Head of Procurement
Neptune Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: subprocessors, UK addendum, and TIA summary for procurement review

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. We can definitely get you what you need by EOD Wednesday. Plan below and attached artifacts: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf (DPA + UK addendum tracked changes) and subprocessor_inventory_20270118.csv.

Quick plan (deliverables & owners):
- Subprocessor inventory (Marcus) — CSV attached; includes vendor name, function, processing location, and last-assessed date.
- Transfer safeguards one-pager (Neha) — summary of SCCs + our UK IDTA approach and TIA coverage for high-risk flows.
- UK addendum redline (Stephanie) — attached tracked-changes docx.
- Attestations — SOC 2 report link and encryption summary included in the DPA appendix.

Suggested MAP milestones (we can adapt):
1) Wed 20 Jan — Redwood provides artifacts and proposed DPA redline
2) Fri 22 Jan — Neptune legal sends redline/comments
3) Mon 25 Jan — 30-min call to resolve open clauses; aim to sign week of Jan 25

We can join the 11:00–12:00 PT slot on Wednesday if that still works for your legal team.

If helpful, Marcus added a short table in the CSV indicating which subprocessors are EU/UK located vs US.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf (DPA + appendix), subprocessor_inventory_20270118.csv (CSV), uk_addendum_tracked_changes.docx (tracked changes doc)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: subprocessors, UK addendum, and TIA summary for procurement review

Stephanie / Neha — quick note on sequencing from an ops perspective:

- The subprocessor CSV flags a couple of items that will need short follow-ups (third-party monitoring vendor in APAC that routes logs through a US aggregator). For procurement, let's call that out as a high-priority TIA item.
- For the transfer safeguards one-pager: recommend we provide a matrix that maps (flow type) -> (legal basis used: SCCs/UK IDTA/TIA) -> (controls: encryption, retention, access) so Neptune can quickly tick boxes during review. Neha, can you mock that matrix?
- If Neptune legal asks for an executed UK IDTA vs redline, we should be prepared to offer either: 1) execute our standard UK addendum; or 2) run a short exception playbook (limited duration) while we agree on wording. Both are acceptable but procurement/legal will want dates.

I also added a suggested MAP milestone: have our Security & Legal available on Fri 22 Jan for a 30-minute focused clause review. That should minimize back-and-forth.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neptune Legal <privacy@neptune-analytics.com>, procurement@neptune-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 14:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: subprocessors, UK addendum, and TIA summary for procurement review

Stephanie — this is great, thank you. Procurement has reviewed the CSV and flagged the APAC monitoring flow Marcus mentioned; Legal would like the TIA summary for that flow specifically and a proposed mitigation timeline if you expect changes.

We reviewed the DPA redline at a high level and have one redline ask from counsel regarding the UK addendum indemnity paragraph — they prefer a softer liability allocation. Can your legal team take a look and propose alternative language?

Next steps from Neptune: we will: 1) review the matrix once received, 2) circulate a single consolidated redline by Fri 22 Jan, and 3) confirm a slot for the clause call (we prefer Fri 22 10:00 PT).

Can Redwood confirm availability for Fri 22 10:00 PT for a 30-min call with Redwood Legal + Security?

Thanks — Lisa
